items.title: Jerry Blumberg Interview, 1961-04-06
items.q: The interviewee (Jerry Blumberg) does not mention Mahalia; the mention is made by the Interviewer in the context of their own experience in Chicago.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah. No, that's something else.

I know in Chicago once when I had a tooth pulled, I was down at Mahalia's. And Mahalia and all of her other relatives and different people there, oh, get some Dr. Tischner's ointment and put that in your tooth. Anything that goes wrong at all, they use Dr. Tischner's for. And Bunk always had a bottle of that. But he'd have all these medicines on his music stand, and he'd sit there sometime for two or three sets. I don't think he'd play one piece. Honestly, he'd sit there all night long rubbing that. But any time…

Yeah, well, he'd hit notes like he'd crack a whip. It was just beautiful precision and cleanliness about his playing. And he played a very buoyant style, kind of bouncy, I guess you'd call it. I don't know. It's pretty hard to really... Yeah, I know it's hard to describe any style. Just put it all into words.
